facts.text: The user asked for analysis of their technical writing style, science, and rhetoric.
The user provided a long technical writing passage about therapeutic ultrasound, penetration depth, and thermal effects.
The user’s passage states that ultrasound penetration depth depends on signal frequency.
The user’s passage states that high-intensity ultrasound is often over 1000W/cm2 and is used for thermal properties.
The user’s passage states that 1 MHz ultrasound can penetrate up to 2.3 to 5 cm.
The user’s passage states that 3 MHz ultrasound can penetrate up to 0.8 to 1.6 cm deep.
The user’s passage states that ultrasound cannot be applied across the skull due to massive attenuation at the skin-bone interface.
The user’s passage states that attenuation causes heat as lost acoustic energy converts into thermal energy.
The user’s passage includes a table comparing NIR light, microwaves, ultrasound, and magnetic fields with penetration depth and spatial resolution values.
The user’s passage states that NIR light has 2mm penetration depth and 0.05mm spatial resolution.
The user’s passage states that microwaves have 50mm penetration depth and 4mm spatial resolution.
The user’s passage states that ultrasound has 30mm penetration depth and 1-2mm spatial resolution.
The user’s passage states that magnetic fields have 50mm penetration depth and 10mm spatial resolution.
The user’s passage states an inverse relationship between penetration depth and spatial resolution in primary signals.
The user’s passage states that NIR light can only penetrate 4.4mm into tissue to stimulate the cerebral cortex.
The user’s passage states that microwaves and TMS can penetrate approximately 50mm into the brain to stimulate the entirety of the cerebrum.
The user’s passage states that NIR light can be focused on a near-nanoscale under ideal conditions.
The user’s passage states that TMS and microwaves can only be focused on a centimeter scale.
The user’s passage states that transcranial Doppler can penetrate 30mm into the brain with millimeter-scale resolution.
The user’s passage proposes combining primary signals using different nFNIs to achieve deep stimulation without sacrificing spatial resolution.
The user’s passage defines nano functional neural interfaces (nFNIs) as nanotransducers that convert a primary external signal to a secondary form of energy that can activate an ion channel.
The user’s passage states that nFNIs can receive secondary energy from an ion channel/neuron and convert it back into the primary form of energy.
The user’s passage states that electromagnetic radiation, ultrasound, and magnetic force are three primary signals used in nFNIs.
The user’s passage states that secondary energy forms can include electrical, magnetic, thermal, optical, and mechanical energies.
The user’s passage includes a table listing seven nano functional neural interfaces with primary signals, secondary signals, materials, and binding targets.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses VIS light as the primary signal and an electric field as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the VIS light nFNI uses quantum dots (CdSe) as the material.
The user’s passage states that the VIS light nFNI targets membrane/intracellular voltage-gated ion channels.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses a magnetic field as the primary signal and an electric field as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field nFNI uses CoFe2O4-BaTiO3 as the material.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field nFNI targets membrane/intracellular voltage-gated ion channels.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses ultrasound as the primary signal and an electric field as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the ultrasound nFNI uses piezocrystals (barium titanate) as the material.
The user’s passage states that the ultrasound nFNI targets membrane/intracellular voltage-gated ion channels.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses VIS/NIR light as the primary signal and heat as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the VIS/NIR light nFNI uses gold nanomaterials as the material.
The user’s passage states that the VIS/NIR light nFNI targets TRPV1 ion channels.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses a magnetic field as the primary signal and heat as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field heat nFNI uses superparamagnetic materials (manganese ferrite) as the material.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field heat nFNI targets TRPV1 ion channels.
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses NIR light as the primary signal and UV/Vis as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the NIR-to-UV/Vis nFNI uses NaYF4:Yb,Er nanoparticles as the material.
The user’s passage states that the NIR-to-UV/Vis nFNI targets light-sensitive ion channels (ChRs, Chrimson, Jaws).
The user’s passage states that one nFNI uses a magnetic field as the primary signal and mechanical force as the secondary signal.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field mechanical-force nFNI uses magnetite nanoparticles as the material.
The user’s passage states that the magnetic-field mechanical-force nFNI targets membrane/mechano-gated ion channels (DEG, K2P).
The user’s passage states that the seven transducers can be grouped into electrotransducers, thermotransducers, optotransducers, and mechanotransducers.
The user’s passage states that optotransducers use optogenetics to stimulate ion channels.
The user’s passage states that optogenetics involves genetically engineered creatures with light-sensitive ion channels called opsins on the plasma membrane or artificially inserted opsins.
The user’s passage states that opsins respond to specific wavelengths of light to inhibit or excite neurons.
The user’s passage states that optotransducers work as stimulators only because light stimulates the ion channel but the ion channel does not produce light.
The user’s passage states that thermotransducers create localized heat from primary signals such as light or magnetic fields.
The user’s passage states that TRP channels, specifically TRPV1, are temperature-gated ion channels effective for thermotransducers.
The user’s passage states that ferrous materials such as manganese ferrite are effective magnetothermal transducers.
The user’s passage states that optoelectronic, magnetoelectric, piezoelectric, and magnetomechanical nanotransducers are explored as options for an nFNI because they are bidirectional.
The user’s passage states that quantum dots (QDs) are semiconducting nanocrystals that transport electrons.
The user’s passage states that cadmium selenide (CdSe) is the most common quantum dot and consists of heavy metal and a nonmetal.
The user’s passage states that QDs can be fine-tuned to emit or absorb wavelengths from ultraviolet to near-infrared due to quantum confinement.
The user’s passage states that quantum confinement occurs when particle size is too small to be comparable to the wavelength of an electron.
The user’s passage states that quantum dots have high photostability and quantum efficiency.
The user’s passage states that quantum dots are used for clinical purposes such as fluorescent labeling, cancer treatment, and drug delivery.
The user’s passage states that QDs can be used as a platform to image and are small enough to travel through the bloodstream.
The user’s passage states that QDs exhibit optoelectric properties to generate photocurrent.
The user’s passage states that once excited, QDs momentarily create an electric dipole moment that induces an electric field.
The user’s passage states that if a QD is coupled with a neuron within 10 nm of the plasma membrane, the electric field may be enough to create an action potential.
The user’s passage states that neurons have a resting voltage of approximately -70 mV.
The user’s passage states that to begin depolarizing and create an action potential, the voltage would need to be raised to -55 mV.
The user’s passage states that the nFNIs would need to transduce 15 mV to cause the neuron to fire.
The user’s passage states that QDs have been used for photovoltaics with a demonstrated macroscale efficiency of 66%.
The user’s passage states that QDs can allow an attenuated signal to generate an action potential but NIR light must reach the transducers to stimulate the QDs.
The user’s passage states that if QD coating is degraded, the heavy metal core could be toxic.
The user’s passage states that QDs have shown cytotoxicity toward cells in vitro due to release of free cadmium.
The user’s passage states that quantum dots have not been shown to be toxic in humans, and further experimentation should be done.

The user’s passage states that magnetic nanoparticles have been investigated for medical applications including magnetic separation of biological entities, nano-drug delivery, cancer treatment, and MRI.
The user’s passage states that magnetic nanoparticles for neural interfacing typically consist of a metallic core paired with a shell for biocompatibility and stability.
The user’s passage states that internal cores can be made from iron-cobalt alloys with a coating that protects from oxidation.
The user’s passage states that magnetoelectric nanoparticles (MENs) and magnetomechanical nanoparticles (MMNs) will be investigated.

The user’s passage states that in a study by Gudurut et al., EEG waveforms of live mice were modulated by 30 nm CoFe2O4-BaTiO3 magnetoelectric core-shell nanoparticles under low energy magnetic fields (20 Oe at 20 Hz).
The user’s passage states that CoFe2O4-BaTiO3 was chosen due to a powerful magneto-electric effect from strain-induced coupling between cobalt ferrite cores and barium titanate shells.

The user’s passage states that in an investigation by Nguyen et al., magnetic nanoparticles localized to a specific region of the brain induced a local electric field of 1000 V/m with roughly 50 mT at 10 Hz.
The user’s passage states that standard transcranial magnetic stimulation requires approximately 1 T to produce a similar effect.
The user’s passage states that in the Gudurut et al. study, cytotoxicity of MENs was performed using glycerol mono-oleate coating.
The user’s passage states that Gudurut et al. found no significant toxicity for human neuron cells in vitro up to 200 μg/ml.
The user’s passage states that MMNs can mechanically modulate cell response and are bound to the plasma membrane using collagen or an equivalent binding protein.
The user’s passage states that MMNs can apply pico-newton forces to stretch ion channels via particle twisting.
The user’s passage states that MMNs can have iron oxide, magnetite, or hematite cores and can have silica, collagen, starch, or dextran coatings.
The user’s passage states that one study demonstrates MMNs targeting mechanosensitive ion channels in cortical neurons.
The user’s passage states that the study used MMNs with magnetite cores coated with starch to target ion channels attempting to cause calcium influx in cortical neurons.
The user’s passage states that using a magnetic field of 110 mT induced a significant calcium influx in transgenic mechanosensitive ion channels.
The user’s passage states that the induced calcium influx required one-tenth of the energy needed to induce calcium influx using TMS.

events.text: The user requested analysis of their technical writing style, science, and rhetoric for the provided passage.
